title: Aflatoxin contamination in staple grains
bottleneck: Aflatoxin — a carcinogenic mold toxin — contaminates maize and groundnuts across the tropics, causing liver cancer and stunting in children, yet most affected countries lack testing infrastructure: contaminated grain is eaten because there's no alternative. Drying and hermetic storage prevent contamination, but adoption is low, and the health damage is chronic and invisible, so urgency is absent. why_it_blocks: A staple food that poisons its consumers is a hidden public-health catastrophe — one of the largest preventable causes of liver cancer worldwide. current_state: Biocontrol with atoxigenic Aspergillus strains works where deployed; most smallholder grain is never tested.
